extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, regulatory attorneys, policy analysts, and rulemaking practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing federal rulemaking, OIRA/OMB review, Regulatory Plans/Unified Agenda, public participation, cost-benefit and peer-review obligations, and executive-order-driven priorities. Covers administrative practice and statutory/EO-driven directives for producing and reviewing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA handling of outside communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Administrator or her designee may receive any outside communications concerning an agency rule that is subject to review. OIRA must forward any such communications to the agency within ten days, invite agency officials to any meetings held with outsiders, and maintain a public log of all such contacts. At the end of the proceeding OIRA must also make available all documents exchanged with the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural transparency and channeling: restrict who may accept outside input to OIRA, ensure prompt forwarding to agencies, involve agency officials in meetings, keep public logs, and disclose exchanged documents after the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Agenda publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue the semiannual publication of the Unified Agenda of Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions, which lists all proposed, pending, and completed regulatory and deregulatory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unified Agenda is a public planning instrument used to announce agency regulatory activities twice a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plans in October Unified Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: The October Agenda must contain each agency’s annual Regulatory Plans, which must be approved personally by the agency head. These plans must be forwarded to OIRA (and then on to affected agencies, the Vice President and a group of named high-level White House Advisors) by June 1 of each year. The plans are supposed to also include agency determinations on which existing rules are to be reviewed and reconsidered during the ensuing year and 'preliminary estimates of the anticipated costs and benefits' of each rule planned for that calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual Regulatory Plans are approved at the top level, forwarded to OIRA by a statutory deadline, and must include planned retrospective reviews and preliminary cost-benefit estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of planning and agenda provisions to independent agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12866, for the first time the independent regulatory agencies are specifically directed to comply with the planning and agenda provisions (though not with the rule-review process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent regulatory agencies must participate in regulatory planning and Unified Agenda requirements even where some review processes differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language directive
rubrics_metrics.description: Presidential directive on plain language (plain language requirement/directive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are instructed to draft regulations in plain language to improve clarity and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA public documentation of implementation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA issued a memorandum describing the 'general principles and procedures that will be applied by OMB in the implementation of Executive Order 12866 and related statutory and executive authority.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA should issue written guidance/memoranda laying out principles and procedures for implementing EO-based review to ensure consistency and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA transparency practices (posting letters and guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA published guidelines and other information on its website and posted public 'return letters' (send rules back to the agency), 'review letters' (comment on aspects of a particular rule review), and 'prompt letters' (suggest new or stronger regulations) on reginfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA practice includes online publication of guidance and review correspondence to promote transparency of the review process (though usage of letters has varied across administrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-4 requirement for regulatory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-4 provides guidance on the development of regulatory analyses (revised in 2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory impact analyses should follow the methods and practices set out in OMB Circular A-4 (e.g., benefits/costs estimation, discounting, sensitivity analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review for influential regulatory information
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Bulletin requires administrative agencies to conduct a peer review on all 'influential regulatory information that the agency intends to disseminate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must subject influential scientific/technical information to peer review before dissemination to ensure scientific integrity and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Guidance Practices bulletin
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB issued a government-wide Bulletin on Good Guidance Practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow prescribed good guidance practices when issuing guidance documents to ensure transparency, notice, and appropriate procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated Principles for Risk Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB (and OSTP) issued a set of Updated Principles for Risk Analysis, updating prior Clinton-era principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should adhere to updated risk analysis principles when assessing risks in regulatory decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of hard-to-quantify values
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies were urged to consider 'values that are difficult or impossible to quantify, including equity, human dignity, fairness, and distributive impacts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory analysis and decisionmaking should account for qualitative and distributional values in addition to monetized benefits and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful online public comment opportunity and 60-day baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Afford the public a meaningful opportunity to comment through the Internet on any proposed regulation, with a comment period that should generally be at least 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internet-based docketing and generally provide 60 days for public comment to ensure ample opportunity for participation, except where shorter periods are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely online access to rulemaking docket and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, for both proposed and final rules, timely online access to the rulemaking docket on regulations.gov, including relevant scientific and technical findings, in an open format that can be easily searched and downloaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make docket materials and supporting information machine-readable and readily accessible to facilitate public review and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment on all pertinent parts of the docket
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed rules, provide 'an opportunity for public comment on all pertinent parts of the rulemaking docket, including relevant scientific and technical findings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the public can comment not only on the proposed regulatory text but also on supporting analyses and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek public input before issuing NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek public input from affected persons 'before issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders early in the regulatory process to inform rule design and reduce reliance on ex post changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider approaches that reduce burdens and preserve flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and consider regulatory approaches that reduce burdens and maintain flexibility and freedom of choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing rules, consider less burdensome alternatives such as performance standards, voluntary approaches, or incentive-based measures that preserve individual choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote retrospective review of existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote retrospective analysis of rules that may be outmoded, ineffective, insufficient, or excessively burdensome, and to modify, streamline, expand, or repeal them in accordance with what has been learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should undertake systematic retrospective review ('lookback') programs to identify and fix ineffective or overly burdensome regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop preliminary plan for periodic review of significant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Within 120 days of the date of this order, . . . develop and submit to [OIRA] a preliminary plan' for periodically reviewing 'its existing significant regulations to determine whether any such regulations should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must create and submit concrete preliminary plans for ongoing retrospective review of significant rules on a schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to review significant guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that 'significant guidance documents' also be reviewed by OIRA in a way similar to significant regulatory actions (added under EO 13422 and later reinstated by memorandum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend formal review processes to major guidance documents to ensure consistency with regulatory priorities and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specific 'market failures' justifying rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies were required to identify in writing specific 'market failures' that necessitate a rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking justifications should expressly state the market failure being addressed to ground the need for regulatory intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Policy Officers as presidential appointees and approvers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Regulatory Policy Officers were to be presidential appointees, and these officers must approve the Regulatory Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate and centralize review approval within agencies by making Regulatory Policy Officers politically appointed and responsible for plan sign-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include aggregate costs and benefits in Regulatory Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that aggregate costs and benefits for all rules must be included in the Regulatory Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Plans should present consolidated estimates of regulatory costs and benefits to facilitate cross-rule prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 'formal' on-the-record rulemaking for complex determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider whether to use 'formal' ('on the record') rulemaking for 'complex determinations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where subject-matter complexity warrants, agencies should evaluate the need for more formal, record-based procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13771 regulatory offset and repeal ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Require agencies to identify at least two regulations to be repealed for every proposed or promulgated regulation. The cost of each new regulation must be fully offset by the repeal specified above, and the agency must provide an approximation of the total costs or savings associated with each new regulation or repealed regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies to constrain regulatory costs: identify offsets, estimate net costs/savings, and track these in budgetary/regulatory planning processes (including Unified Agenda inclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB guidance on measuring regulatory costs and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: The OMB Director must provide agencies with guidance addressing the processes for measuring regulatory costs, the costs of existing regulations, what qualifies as new and offsetting regulations, and situations that would require waivers of the order’s requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized methodological guidance and waiver procedures are to be issued by OMB to operationalize offset requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Regulatory Reform Officer and Task Forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the head of each agency to designate an official as its Regulatory Reform Officer (RRO) and form a Regulatory Reform Task Force (composition specified for agencies listed in 31 U.S.C. § 901(b)(1)) to evaluate existing regulations and make recommendations to the agency head regarding their repeal, replacement, or modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must create internal structures (RRO + Task Force) to carry out regulatory reform and retrospective review responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Force prioritization criteria for scrutinizing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In making determinations, the task forces should focus on regulations that: (1) 'eliminate jobs, or inhibit job creation;' (2) 'are outdated, unnecessary, or ineffective;' (3) 'impose costs that exceed benefits;' (4) 'create serious inconsistency or otherwise interfere with regulatory initiatives and policies;' (5) 'are inconsistent with the requirements of section 515 ... in particular those regulations that rely in whole or in part on data, information, or methods that are not publicly available or that are insufficiently transparent to meet the standard for reproducibility;' or (6) 'derive from or implement Executive Orders or other Presidential directives that have been subsequently rescinded or substantially modified.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific substantive screens for prioritizing candidate regulations for repeal/revision under reform task forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy-related regulatory review (EO 13783)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct agencies to review regulations that 'potentially burden the development or use of domestically produced energy resources and appropriately suspend, revise, or rescind those that unduly burden the development of domestic energy resources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Energy-focused deregulatory screen: assess and act upon regulations that impede domestic energy production or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action threshold ($200M) (EO 14094)
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 14094 reaffirmed and amended EO 12866 § 3(f)’s definition of 'significant regulatory action' to require OIRA review for rulemakings having an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated monetary threshold ($200M annual effect) as a trigger for OIRA review and elevated analytic expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biden modernization reforms for Circular A-4 and distributional analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Modernizing Regulatory Review memorandum directs recommendations that should include concrete suggestions on how the regulatory review process can 'promote public health and safety, economic growth, social welfare, racial justice, environmental stewardship, human dignity, equity, and the interests of future generations,' including proposed reforms to Circular A-4 to promote these goals; suggest procedures that take into account distributional impacts in regulatory analyses; propose how OIRA can partner with agencies to 'explore, promote, and undertake regulatory initiatives that are likely to yield significant benefits'; and determine an appropriate approach to the review of guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernization entails broadening analytic frameworks (distributional impacts, equity), revised A-4 guidance, proactive OIRA-agency collaboration, and clarified guidance-review protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement/revocation of Circular A-4 (EO 14192)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 14192 revoked OMB Circular No. A-4 of November 9, 2023, and reinstated the prior, September 17, 2003, version of OMB Circular No. A-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification of which version of OMB Circular A-4 agencies must follow is a directive-level requirement that affects analytic methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand OIRA review to independent agencies and establish performance standards (EO 14215)
rubrics_metrics.description: This directive expands the review authority, for proposed and final significant rulemakings, of OIRA to include independent regulatory agencies. It also directs the OMB Director to 'establish performance standards and management objectives' for independent agency leadership and periodically update the President on performance and efficiency of these agencies and their heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadened jurisdictional scope of OIRA review and introduction of performance management expectations for independent agencies' leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOGE Team consultation and legal-consistency review (EO 14219)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs agency heads to work with their DOGE Team Leads and the OMB Director to review all regulations subject to their jurisdiction for consistency with law and the current Administration’s policy. Agency heads must identify regulations that are, among other things, unconstitutional, raising serious constitutional difficulties, based on unlawful delegations, impose costs to private parties that are not outweighed by public benefit, and impose undue burdens on small business. These identified regulations would then be added, in consultation with OIRA, to an agency’s Unified Regulatory Agenda for modification or rescission. The order further directs enforcement to de-prioritize actions that are based on 'anything other than the best reading of a statute' and requires consultation with DOGE Team Leads on potential new regulations as soon as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New compliance/legal-consistency screen: agencies must coordinate with designated DOGE teams and OMB to identify legally vulnerable or economically unjustified rules and place them on reform agendas; enforcement priorities and consultation timelines are also specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA-issued memoranda and guidance for implementing Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA issued memoranda (e.g., September 2001 memorandum, guidance implementing EO 13771, and a July 19, 2023 memorandum) to describe principles, procedures, and guidance for how to implement Executive Orders and related regulatory-review requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow OIRA memoranda and implementation guidance as the operationalization of EO directives (e.g., on timelines, cost measurement, and procedural expectations).
